provenance.author: block writer B6 (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Codex review 2026-10-18 applied: C5 model 'yn elyn'; s092 'Ofynnodd y negesydd am fwyd?'; C1 'yn ei gasglu'; A3/A4/A6 accept colloquial fod e / bod hi; A7 accepts a / os ydy (no compulsory backshift; explanation added); nodyn_en distinguishes full and colloquial pronoun forms; s018 'Fydda i byth yn eillio …'; s033 'ond roedd un ochr yn fyr iawn'. Verdicts recorded on all review questions.

Target G33 is narrowed to one core: bod-reporting after a past verb. Reported statements (dwedodd X fod …, ei fod e …, ei bod hi …) and reported yes/no questions (gofynnodd X a / os oedd …) occur about 30 times, mostly in three retelling scenes: the morning council, Mali's retelling to Modlen (who missed the messenger) and Mali's diary. Each reported sentence has its direct-speech original earlier in the chapter, so the contrast meddai ↔ dwedodd … fod is built from the chapter itself.

y byddai appears once (Mali to Modlen), glossed '= "bydd …" (ddoe)' and immediately followed by the direct quotation of the threat ('Ei eiriau fe oedd: Bydd Rhita'n dod!'); it is listed as an incidental and is never tested.
Dafi's one deliberate error ('dwedodd e bod rhyfel yn dod') contrasts with the chapter target (dwedodd + fod) and is corrected by Mali at once.

Open-slot words (CorCenCC top 2000): erbyn (302) and neu (37) for the plan's demand 'Anfon dy farf erbyn y lleuad newydd, neu bydd Rhita'n dod!'; darn (442) for the lock of Cynyr's beard (the 'deposit' is shown as 'Dyma'r dechrau … darn o farf Cynyr nawr, a barf y brenin wedyn' rather than with a word for deposit); achos (576) because Mali's and Arthur's reasons need it. neb is already known from Pennod 26's open slots.
Form added: dwedodd (cy-dweud) and gofynnodd (cy-gofyn), preterite 3sg, already licensed at 33 by the plan's new_forms.

Continuity: Rhita's cloak shows the beards of the kings of Iwerddon (red) and Llydaw (black), matching Pennod 37 as written. The messenger cuts a long gold lock from one side of Cynyr's beard and takes it away with the cloak (Mali recovers it in 37). The deadline is the new moon, two weeks away (Mali). Modlen missed the messenger (she was in the kitchen) and decides on a wool beard; nothing in this chapter decides the plan or the journey (34).

Checker warnings justified: 'a oedd' lint-a-ac hits are the interrogative particle a in reported questions (gofynnodd e a oedd …), not the conjunction; three local-density warnings fall in Mali's retelling and the council, where this chapter's own words (bygwth, bygythiad, rhyfel, heddwch, rhybuddio) recur after being introduced and glossed earlier in the chapter; the near-duplicate pair is Mali's correction of Dafi's deliberate error and his corrected repeat.

Length about 1,530 words against 1,690 (window from 1,521): the chapter ends on Mali's diary and Modlen sewing; no padding added. Mean sentence length is kept in the Rhan 4 window by splitting only very long multi-sentence turns.

primary_new_grammar.label: Reported speech after a past verb: dwedodd X fod … / ei fod e … / ei bod hi …; reported yes/no questions gofynnodd X a / os oedd …; y byddai met once as a glossed recognition-only phrase beside the directly quoted threat (Bydd Rhita'n dod!)

cover.alt: In the great hall at Caerllion the huge messenger holds up the long cloak of beards before the throne; the hall laughs at the beardless boy-king.
cover.art_brief: The great hall of the castle at Caerllion at night (Caerllion palette: red brick and timber, torches, a big hearth, a red-dragon banner on green and white). Rhita's messenger (a huge man, taller than the doorway, long grey snow-dusted hooded cloak, big boots, broad pale face) stands in the middle of the hall holding up the cloak of beards (long tufts of beard hair in red, gold, black, grey and white stitched together in rows; no faces; comic, never gory) so that it hangs down to his boots, pointing with one big finger at a red beard and a long black beard on it. On the tall throne Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest) wearing the too-big gold crown sits very straight with a smooth, beardless face. Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak, sword at his belt) beside the throne is laughing; lords and knights round the tables laugh behind their hands; Cynyr (broad, huge golden-blond beard to mid-chest, brown cloak with round silver brooch) frowns and holds his huge golden beard. Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, satchel) stands by the throne, serious. Myrddin (very old, thin, long white beard, round wire spectacles, patched deep-blue robe, tall black brimmed hat) watches from the hearth, a wisp of smoke from his hat. No text.

segments.text: Safodd y negesydd enfawr ar ei draed, ac roedd ei ben e'n agos at y to.
"Arglwyddi!" meddai e mewn llais mawr, dwfn. "Dyma neges Rhita Gawr, y cawr mwyaf yn Eryri."
segments.speaker: char-negesydd-rhita

segments.text: Cododd e'r clogyn barfau o'r llawr, ac roedd y barfau'n cyrraedd ei draed e.
"Mae Rhita'n casglu barfau," meddai'r negesydd. "Barfau brenhinoedd! Dyma farf brenin Iwerddon: barf goch. A dyma farf brenin Llydaw: barf ddu, hir."
segments.speaker: char-negesydd-rhita

segments.text: "Mae Rhita wedi gorchfygu llawer o frenhinoedd, ac mae e wedi cymryd eu barfau nhw.
Mae Rhita'n mynnu cael barf gan bob brenin."
"Ond dyw'r clogyn ddim yn barod eto. Mae Rhita eisiau barf y brenin newydd i orffen y clogyn."

inference_aids.gloss: i orffen ← gorffen: gwneud yn barod

segments.text: Edrychodd y negesydd ar Arthur, ac wedyn dwedodd e'r neges yn uchel iawn:
"Frenin Arthur! Anfon dy farf at Rhita Gawr erbyn y lleuad newydd, neu bydd Rhita'n dod!"
segments.speaker: char-negesydd-rhita

segments.text: "Bydd e'n dod gyda byddin o gewri, a bydd rhyfel yng Nghymru!"
Roedd y neuadd yn dawel iawn. Wedyn edrychodd pawb ar wyneb y brenin newydd: wyneb bachgen, heb farf.
Dechreuodd Cai chwerthin. Wedyn dechreuodd y marchogion chwerthin, a'r arglwyddi barfog, a'r morynion. Roedd pawb yn y neuadd yn chwerthin.
"Barf?" meddai Cai. "Does dim barf gyda Arthur! Mae mwy o farf gyda Pero!"
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: Ond yn sydyn, doedd neb yn chwerthin. Doedd neb eisiau gweld byddin o gewri yng Nghymru.
Cododd Arthur o'r orsedd, ac roedd ei draed e ar y llawr nawr.
"Diolch am y neges," meddai'r brenin. "Ond does dim barf gyda fi. Mae pawb yn gallu gweld hynny."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Wel, un diwrnod bydd barf gyda ti," meddai'r negesydd. "Wedyn rhaid i ti ei heillio hi, a'i hanfon hi at Rhita."
segments.speaker: char-negesydd-rhita

segments.text: "Na," meddai Arthur. "Fydda i byth yn eillio fy marf i i gawr balch."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Gwrthododd Arthur, ac roedd y neuadd yn dawel eto.
"Rwyt ti'n gwrthod?" meddai'r negesydd. "Mae Rhita'n bygwth rhyfel, frenin bach! Mae e'n gawr peryglus iawn."
segments.speaker: char-negesydd-rhita

segments.text: "Dw i eisiau heddwch," meddai Arthur, "ond dw i ddim yn ofni dy fygythiad di.
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Dyw barf ddim yn bwysig.
Mae heddwch yn bwysig."
Edrychodd y negesydd ar y neuadd. Wedyn gwelodd e farf fawr, aur Cynyr, a gwenodd e.
"Does dim barf gyda'r brenin," meddai e. "Ond mae barf gyda'r arglwydd hwn!"
segments.speaker: char-negesydd-rhita

segments.text: Yn sydyn, tynnodd e gyllell, a thorrodd e ddarn hir o farf Cynyr.

inference_aids.alt: The messenger cuts a long lock from one side of Cynyr's huge golden beard with a knife while Cynyr stares in horror and the lords leap up.
inference_aids.art_brief: Close scene in the same hall at Caerllion (torchlight, red brick, timber). Rhita's messenger (a huge man, taller than the doorway, long grey snow-dusted hooded cloak, big boots, broad pale face) leans over Cynyr (broad, huge golden-blond beard to mid-chest, brown cloak with round silver brooch) and with a short knife cuts a long golden lock from one side of his huge beard, grinning; the lock hangs from his big fist. Cynyr's mouth is open in horror; one side of his beard is now short. Behind them an big red-bearded lord (Barf Goch) clutches his own beard; Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest) (crown, blue robe) has risen from the throne with one hand raised; Elen (about fifty, white linen veil, forest-green dress, ring of keys) reaches towards Cynyr. The cloak of beards is slung over the messenger's shoulder. No text.

inference_aids.art_brief: The big castle kitchen at Caerllion in the morning (warm firelight, a big bread oven, copper pots, stacked clean dishes). Modlen (short, round, rosy, white headscarf, long floury apron, big wooden spoon) has opened a big basket of white and black wool (the wool from the fair) and holds a thick bundle of black wool under her nose and chin like a huge black beard, eyebrows raised, wooden spoon in her other hand. Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, satchel) laughs with her wax tablet under her arm; Dafi (cup-sized red dragon, two short cream horns, tiny bat wings, big yellow eyes; small enough to sit in a wooden drinking cup) sits on top of the warm oven laughing, a puff of grey smoke from his nose. In the doorway Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest) (no crown, blue robe) and Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak, sword at his belt) stare. No text.
